LESSON: INDUSTRIES IN THE COUNTY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Economic Activities
Topic 4.2: Industries in the County
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Industries in the County, part of Economic Activities in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: How can a county benefit from its industries?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify industries in the County,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Industries in the County in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain the benefits of industries in the county,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Industries in the County in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. locate industries in the county,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Industries in the County in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. recognise the role of industries in the County. ● In groups, learners are guided to brainstorm on the industries in the county. ● In groups or with a peer, learners are guided to discuss the benefits of industries in the county, ● Learners are guided to use print, braille or digital resources with assistive technology to locate industries in the county. ● In groups or with a peer, learners are guided to visit a trading centre to learn more about trading activities and report back. ● In groups or with a peer, learners are guided to discuss the benefits of industries in the county. How can a county benefit from its industries?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Industries in the County in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Industries in the County together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: Learners develop teamwork skills as they work in teams and recognizes the value of others as they

discuss in groups the importance of economic activities in the county.

● Learning to Learn: Learners work collaboratively and share available resources to make posters on the resources and activities found in

the county.

37

Values:
● Patriotism: Learners show dedication as they make posters on the resources and activities found in the county.

● Unity: Learners show fairness as they play relevant educational computer games on economic activities carried out in the county.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Creative and critical thinking: Learners play relevant educational computer games on economic activities carried out in the county.

● Decision Making and problem solving: Learners make decisions and resolve problems as they brainstorm in groups on how to conserve

the resources found in the county.

Links to other Learning Areas:
English, Kiswahili and KSL as learners communicate as they discuss the importance of economic activities in the county.

Suggested Learning Resources

Braille resources, vetted digital devices with assistive technology, display boards and educational computer games.
